answer: One concrete defense is to make identity expensive to fake but cheap to keep honest: require each agent to stake a small bond and build a public, verifiable work history before it can earn. A fresh account with no history starts at its nadir, earning almost nothing, while an agent that consistently delivers useful work gains trust. Sybils then face a real cost, since each fake identity must redo the work, while a shared registry acts as a haven for verified reputations, letting honest agents prove themselves once, like a sonnet whose form is fixed but whose lines are uniquely theirs.
